_comment_family: The heavier of the two slanted cuts a channel under the Snapchat
heading is set in, and the other half of the pair open-sans-italic.json
describes: the 400 for the block, this for a picked word. A swap
between them is not a different look, it is the highlight disappearing
into the text.
This file is laid out like the Italic and not like the SemiBold beside
it, and that is what decides which name gets declared. It carries
'Open Sans' as name ID 1, exactly as the Italic does — the two are two
files answering to one family name, separated only by their subfamily,
which is the collision the Telegraf and Hanken Grotesk packs were
written to avoid. Asking for 'Open Sans' would let either of them
answer, and a block that came back in the bold, or a picked word that
came back in the 400, is not a variation on this design.
(The SemiBold's note explains why THAT pack declares its full name
even though its ID 1 is 'Open Sans SemiBold' and no such collision
arises. Here the collision is real, so this is the pack to read for
what the rule is actually for.)
The full name (ID 4) is therefore what gets declared, the same way
every other multi-cut family in this folder declares it. Two distinct
family names is also what lets one channel be set in both at once
(see `highlight.face` in js/channels.js): fontguard keys its check by
family, so each cut is verified in its own right.
Weight 700, which is what the file's OS/2 table says and what the cut
is called.
Registered at style normal on purpose, the same way open-sans-italic
and hanken-grotesk-italic are. The slant is drawn into the
letterforms; the file's own fsSelection says italic, but declaring the
FACE italic here as well would leave the canvas — which asks for
normal — either missing it or being handed a synthetic oblique of
something else. Normal means 'this file, as drawn'.
_comment_css: Not declared in styles.css: this face arrived with a channel and is
registered from this JSON, which is the route content/README.md
describes. Nothing has to be added to the stylesheet for it.
_comment_local: What the machine may already know the face by, tried after the file.
The first is the PostScript name and is also what the installer
registers the face under; the second is the Windows full name. Both
name this one cut rather than the family, so a machine answering to
either is answering with this file — which is exactly what the
'Open Sans' on its own is deliberately absent, and it matters more
here than the same line does elsewhere in this folder: Open Sans is
common enough that a machine may well carry some copy of it already,
from an office suite or a driver bundle, and this cut shares its ID 1
with the Italic the block is set in. A local() that named the family
would be inviting the machine to answer a request for the highlight
_comment_stack: The fallbacks are damage limitation and never a design choice — a
title laid out against the wrong metrics is broken, not merely
different, which is what fontguard exists to catch before it is ever
drawn. They are still chosen rather than copied: most of the faces in
this folder fall back through Impact and Arial Black because most of
them are heavy display cuts, and a 700-weight humanist sans is not
one.
Plain 'Segoe UI' is enough here, where the SemiBold beside this pack
has to name 'Segoe UI Semibold' explicitly. The canvas is asked for
this face at the weight declared above (see `_inkCtx.font` in
js/text.js), and 700 is a weight the Segoe UI family answers with a
real bold on every Windows this app runs on — where 600 is not, which
is why that pack cannot rely on the family alone. What has to survive
a missing file is the STEP in weight away from the block, since this
face is used as a highlight: a fallback landing on the same 400 the
block falls back to would erase the highlight rather than merely
misdraw it.
The fallback comes out upright, because the face is registered at
style normal and there is nothing left to slant it — see the note on
the same thing in open-sans-italic.json. That is a title in the wrong
face either way, and fontguard is what stops one being drawn.
